ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the inclination angle of the slope is $30^{\circ}$. A small ball is thrown horizontally from point $A$ directly above point $B$ at the bottom of the slope with an initial velocity $v_{0}=10\mathrm{m/s}$. The ball hits the slope perpendicularly. Find: 1. The time $t$ from when the small ball is thrown until it hits the inclined plane. 2. The height $h$ of $AB$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, point B is at the bottom end of the inclined plane, A is directly above B, and AB is the vertical height h; the small ball is thrown horizontally to the right from A, and the initial velocity is labeled v0; the inclined plane goes from B upward to the right to D, and the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal bottom side BC is labeled 30°. Then reason: According to the specified method, take B as the origin, the x-axis horizontally to the right, and the y-axis vertically upward. The motion equations of the small ball are x=v0 t, y=h-1/2 g t^2; the velocity at collision is (v0,-gt). Because the small ball collides perpendicularly with the inclined plane whose inclination angle is 30°, the angle between the velocity direction and the horizontal is -60°, so gt/v0=tan60°=sqrt(3). Take v0=10 m/s, g=10 m/s^2, obtaining t=sqrt(3) s. The collision point is on the inclined plane and satisfies y=x tan30°; substituting gives h-1/2 g t^2=(v0 t)tan30°, so h=v0 t tan30°+1/2 g t^2=10*sqrt(3)*(1/sqrt(3))+1/2*10*(sqrt(3))^2=10+15=25 m.
